9	/-!
10	# No-leak over a shrunken base, with no fibre hypothesis
11	
12	The certificate assemblers consume, per piece `j`, the fibrewise clause
13	
14	`∀ s, (fibre over s) ∩ closure (supp ∩ pieces j) ⊆ pieces j`
15	
16	(`isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning`), equivalently emptiness of the **leak locus**
17	`supportLeak (pieces j) = closure (supp ∩ pieces j) \ pieces j`
18	(`Scheme.LocalEquations.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty`).
19	
20	The `tube-fibre` leaf of the DD-R lane tried to obtain this by putting the whole support
21	inside a single piece.  That shape is refuted — `DivSchemeCertZarSep.lean`,
22	`not_exists_unique_support_piece`: both pinned charts carry a partition of unity, so a
23	support point of `V₀ ⊓ V₁` always lies in two distinct pieces.
24	
25	This file gets the clause a different way, and **without any fibre analysis**.  The leak
26	locus is closed, and under a universally closed structure morphism its base image is closed
27	too (`isClosed_image_supportLeak`).  So:
28	
29	* over the *open complement* of that base image, nothing leaks;
30	* that complement is a Zariski neighbourhood of every base point it contains, refinable to a
31	  basic open — the `Localization.Away` shape the pointwise gate consumes.
32	
33	The leak locus is a genuine obstruction only over its own base image, which is a **closed**
34	subset of `Spec R`. So the no-leak clause is available on a Zariski-dense open of the base
35	for free; what a fibre analysis is still needed for is the base points *inside* that closed
36	image.
37	
38	## Main declarations
39	
40	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.exists_basicOpen_supportLeak_eq_empty` — a basic
41	  open around any base point outside the leak's image, over which nothing leaks.
42	* `Scheme.LocalEquations.forall_fibre_closure_subset_of_supportLeak_inter_eq_empty` —
43	  leak-freeness over an open of the base gives the assembler's fibrewise clause there.
44	-/

47	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

54	namespace AlgebraicGeometry

56	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
57	
58	/-! ## The idempotent brick
59	
60	I-0209 predicted the shape of the missing construction: the canonical idempotents of a
61	finite projective colength algebra split the divisor scheme into packets, and a piece
62	swallowing a packet has a clopen trace, hence carries the certificate.  The algebraic core
63	of that is elementary and is recorded here: cutting by an idempotent produces a **direct
64	summand**, so projectivity is inherited with no flatness or finiteness input. -/
65	
66	section Idempotent
67	
68	variable {R B : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing B] [Algebra R B]
69	
70	set_option maxHeartbeats 1000000 in
71	-- The `Ideal`-to-`Submodule` coercion in the quotient makes `liftQ` elaboration expensive.
72	/-- **Cutting by an idempotent gives a direct summand.** For `e` idempotent, multiplication
73	by `e` is a well-defined `R`-linear section of `B ↠ B ⧸ (1 - e)`, so the quotient is a
74	retract of `B` and inherits projectivity.
75	
76	This is the algebraic core of the packet-splitting construction I-0209 asks for: an
77	idempotent of the colength algebra cuts out a clopen packet, and the corresponding quotient
78	is projective for free. -/
79	theorem Module.Projective.quotient_span_singleton_one_sub_of_isIdempotentElem
80	    [Module.Projective R B] (e : B) (he : IsIdempotentElem e) :
81	    Module.Projective R (B ⧸ (Ideal.span {1 - e}).restrictScalars R) := by
82	  set P := (Ideal.span {1 - e}).restrictScalars R with hP
83	  set s : (B ⧸ P) →ₗ[R] B :=
84	    P.liftQ (LinearMap.mulLeft R e) (by
85	      intro x hx
86	      have hx' : x ∈ Ideal.span {1 - e} := hx
87	      rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton] at hx'
88	      obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := hx'
89	      change e * ((1 - e) * c) = 0
90	      rw [← mul_assoc, mul_sub, mul_one, he.eq, sub_self, zero_mul]) with hs
91	  refine Module.Projective.of_split s P.mkQ (LinearMap.ext fun y => ?_)
92	  obtain ⟨b, rfl⟩ := P.mkQ_surjective y
93	  change P.mkQ (e * b) = P.mkQ b
94	  rw [← sub_eq_zero, ← map_sub, Submodule.mkQ_apply, Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero]
95	  change e * b - b ∈ Ideal.span {1 - e}
96	  rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton]
97	  exact ⟨-b, by ring⟩
98	
99	set_option maxHeartbeats 1000000 in
100	-- Same elaboration cost as the projective companion.
101	/-- **The flat companion.** A retract of a flat module is flat, so an idempotent cut also
102	inherits flatness.  This is the form that applies to the DD-R pieces: the piece section
103	rings `Γ(relCurve C R, pieces j)` are known **flat** over `R` (localizations of the free
104	pinned-chart rings, `FinCoverData.flat_sections_pieces`) rather than projective, so it is
105	this version that discharges the (c1) input from a packet idempotent. -/
106	theorem Module.Flat.quotient_span_singleton_one_sub_of_isIdempotentElem
107	    [Module.Flat R B] (e : B) (he : IsIdempotentElem e) :
108	    Module.Flat R (B ⧸ (Ideal.span {1 - e}).restrictScalars R) := by
109	  set P := (Ideal.span {1 - e}).restrictScalars R with hP
110	  set s : (B ⧸ P) →ₗ[R] B :=
111	    P.liftQ (LinearMap.mulLeft R e) (by
112	      intro x hx
113	      have hx' : x ∈ Ideal.span {1 - e} := hx
114	      rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton] at hx'
115	      obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := hx'
116	      change e * ((1 - e) * c) = 0
117	      rw [← mul_assoc, mul_sub, mul_one, he.eq, sub_self, zero_mul]) with hs
118	  exact Module.Flat.of_retract s P.mkQ (LinearMap.ext fun y => by
119	    obtain ⟨b, rfl⟩ := P.mkQ_surjective y
120	    change P.mkQ (e * b) = P.mkQ b
121	    rw [← sub_eq_zero, ← map_sub, Submodule.mkQ_apply, Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero]
122	    change e * b - b ∈ Ideal.span {1 - e}
123	    rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton]
124	    exact ⟨-b, by ring⟩)
125	
126	end Idempotent

128	namespace Scheme.LocalEquations

130	variable {X : Scheme.{u}} {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (d : X.LocalEquations)
131	
132	/-- **A leak-free basic open around any base point outside the leak's image.** The leak
133	locus is closed and its base image is closed under a universally closed morphism, so the
134	complement is open; refining it to a basic open (`PrimeSpectrum.isTopologicalBasis_basic_opens`)
135	gives the `Localization.Away` shape the pointwise certificate gate consumes. -/
136	theorem exists_basicOpen_supportLeak_eq_empty (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of R))
137	    [UniversallyClosed f] (U : X.Opens) {p : PrimeSpectrum R}
138	    (hp : (p : Spec (CommRingCat.of R)) ∉ f.base '' d.supportLeak U) :
139	    ∃ r : R, r ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
140	      f.base ⁻¹' (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen r : Set (PrimeSpectrum R))
141	        ∩ d.supportLeak U = ∅ := by
142	  classical
143	  have hopen : IsOpen ((f.base '' d.supportLeak U)ᶜ) :=
144	    (d.isClosed_image_supportLeak f U).isOpen_compl
145	  obtain ⟨W, hWmem, hpW, hWsub⟩ :=
146	    PrimeSpectrum.isTopologicalBasis_basic_opens.exists_subset_of_mem_open
147	      (a := p) hp hopen
148	  obtain ⟨r, rfl⟩ := hWmem
149	  refine ⟨r, (PrimeSpectrum.mem_basicOpen r p).mp hpW, ?_⟩
150	  rw [Set.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem]
151	  rintro x ⟨hxb, hxl⟩
152	  exact hWsub hxb ⟨x, hxl, rfl⟩
153	
154	/-- **Leak-freeness over a base open gives the assembler's fibrewise clause there.** If no
155	point over the base set `V` leaks out of `U`, then for every base point `s ∈ V` the fibre of
156	the closure of the *restricted* trace stays in `U`.
157	
158	This is the bridge from the closed-image mechanism to the shape
159	`finite_colength_of_forall_fibre_closure_subset` consumes: the closure is taken of the trace
160	restricted over `V`, which only shrinks it, so a leak would have to be a leak of the
161	unrestricted trace. -/
162	theorem forall_fibre_closure_subset_of_supportLeak_inter_eq_empty
163	    (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)) (U : X.Opens) {V : Set (Spec (CommRingCat.of R))}
164	    (hV : f.base ⁻¹' V ∩ d.supportLeak U = ∅) :
165	    ∀ s ∈ V, f.base ⁻¹' {s}
166	        ∩ closure (d.supportLocus ∩ (U : Set X) ∩ f.base ⁻¹' V)
167	      ⊆ (U : Set X) := by
168	  intro s hs x hx
169	  by_contra hxU
170	  -- `x` is in the closure of the full trace, and outside `U`, hence a leak
171	  have hcl : x ∈ closure (d.supportLocus ∩ (U : Set X)) :=
172	    closure_mono Set.inter_subset_left hx.2
173	  have hxV : x ∈ f.base ⁻¹' V := by
174	    have : f.base x = s := hx.1
175	    rw [Set.mem_preimage, this]; exact hs
176	  exact Set.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem.mp hV x ⟨hxV, hcl, hxU⟩
177	
178	/-! ## No-leak IS the Z-clopen condition
179	
180	The recorded design constraint of this project (memory I-0209, "the Z-clopen certificate
181	principle") says a piece carries an `R`-finite colength exactly when its trace on the divisor
182	scheme is *clopen* in that scheme.  The following two lemmas identify that principle with the
183	leak locus, so the two vocabularies are the same statement:
184	
185	the piece trace `supp ∩ U` is always **open** in the subspace `supp` (as `U` is open), so it
186	is clopen there precisely when it is closed in the ambient space — precisely when nothing
187	leaks. -/
188	
189	/-- **Leak-freeness is clopen-ness of the trace in the support.** The forward direction of
190	the identification with the Z-clopen principle (I-0209). -/
191	theorem isClopen_trace_of_supportLeak_eq_empty (U : X.Opens)
192	    (h : d.supportLeak U = ∅) :
193	    IsClopen ((fun x : d.supportLocus => x.val) ⁻¹' (U : Set X)) := by
194	  have hclosed : IsClosed (d.supportLocus ∩ (U : Set X)) :=
195	    (d.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty U).mpr h
196	  refine ⟨?_, U.isOpen.preimage continuous_subtype_val⟩
197	  have heq : (fun x : d.supportLocus => x.val) ⁻¹' (U : Set X)
198	      = (fun x : d.supportLocus => x.val) ⁻¹' (d.supportLocus ∩ (U : Set X)) := by
199	    ext x; simp
200	  rw [heq]
201	  exact hclosed.preimage continuous_subtype_val
202	
203	/-- The converse: a clopen trace leaks nothing.  Together with the previous lemma, the
204	assembler's per-piece no-leak clause and the Z-clopen principle of I-0209 are literally the
205	same condition — so the certificate lane's finiteness obligation was never about fibres, it
206	was about the trace being a connected-component-like piece of the divisor scheme. -/
207	theorem supportLeak_eq_empty_of_isClopen_trace (U : X.Opens)
208	    (h : IsClosed ((fun x : d.supportLocus => x.val) ⁻¹' (U : Set X))) :
209	    d.supportLeak U = ∅ := by
210	  refine (d.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty U).mp ?_
211	  -- a set closed in the closed subspace `supp` is closed in `X`
212	  obtain ⟨T, hT, hTeq⟩ := (isClosed_induced_iff (f := fun x : d.supportLocus => x.val)).mp h
213	  have heq : d.supportLocus ∩ (U : Set X) = d.supportLocus ∩ T := by
214	    ext x
215	    constructor
216	    · rintro ⟨hxs, hxU⟩
217	      exact ⟨hxs, (Set.ext_iff.mp hTeq ⟨x, hxs⟩).mpr hxU⟩
218	    · rintro ⟨hxs, hxT⟩
219	      exact ⟨hxs, (Set.ext_iff.mp hTeq ⟨x, hxs⟩).mp hxT⟩
220	  rw [heq]
221	  exact d.isClosed_supportLocus.inter hT
222	
223	end Scheme.LocalEquations
224	
225	/-! ## The (c1) clause from a clopen trace
226	
227	Assembling the identification with the landed finiteness engine: a clopen piece trace gives
228	the assembler's `hnoLeak` at that piece, hence its `Module.Finite` colength.  Combined with
229	`SupportTube.projective_colength_of_forall_tmul_residueField` this is the whole (c1) input,
230	so under the Z-clopen hypothesis the certificate's finiteness side needs no fibre analysis.
231	
232	What remains outstanding for the lane is only the *production* of the clopen trace, i.e.
233	I-0209's `W`-as-algebra extraction. `PrimeSpectrum.isClopen_iff_zeroLocus` and
234	`PrimeSpectrum.exists_idempotent_basicOpen_eq_of_isClopen` are the mathlib translations that
235	turn a clopen packet of the divisor scheme into the idempotent the brick above consumes. -/
236	
237	section Clopen
238	
239	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))} [IsProper C.hom]
240	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
241	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi]
242	variable {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
243	
244	namespace DivisorAdaptation
245	
246	variable (A : DivisorAdaptation C R pi d)
247	
248	/-- **A clopen piece trace gives the (c1)-finite clause at that piece.** Reading the
249	identification `supportLeak = ∅ ↔ clopen trace` into the landed finiteness engine
250	`finite_colength_of_supportLeak_eq_empty`. -/
251	theorem finite_colength_of_isClopen_trace (j : A.index)
252	    (h : IsClosed ((fun x : d.supportLocus => x.val) ⁻¹'
253	      (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)))) :
254	    Module.Finite R (A.colength j) :=
255	  A.finite_colength_of_supportLeak_eq_empty j
256	    (d.supportLeak_eq_empty_of_isClopen_trace _ h)
257	
258	/-- **The full (c1) data at a piece with clopen trace.** Finiteness from the clopen trace,
259	projectivity from fibrewise regularity of the piece equation — which for a seed adaptation
260	is landed (`ThetaGeneratorSeed.divisorAdaptation_fibre_regular`).  No fibre containment and
261	no flatness of a Čech cokernel enters. -/
262	theorem finite_and_projective_colength_of_isClopen_trace [IsNoetherianRing R] (j : A.index)
263	    (h : IsClosed ((fun x : d.supportLocus => x.val) ⁻¹'
264	      (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))))
265	    (hreg : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
266	      (A.eqn j ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
267	          Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces j) ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ∈
268	        nonZeroDivisors
269	          (Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces j) ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
270	    Module.Finite R (A.colength j) ∧ Module.Projective R (A.colength j) := by
271	  haveI := A.finite_colength_of_isClopen_trace j h
272	  exact ⟨‹_›, A.projective_colength_of_forall_tmul_residueField j hreg⟩

7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeCertZarKerSpan
8	
9	/-!
10	# The certificate of a support-separated adaptation
11	
12	The DD-R certificate lane was built around the equalizer `W(d) = ker (δ_left − δ_right)`
13	of the two overlap-restriction arrows.  Its two flat-cokernel clauses (c3)/(c4), and the
14	kernel-spanning input of `isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning`, are the genuinely hard
15	relative content — `DivSchemeHighWindowSyzygy.lean` shows the kernel-spanning law is
16	*equivalent* to the flatness one is trying to prove, so no cleverer submodule evades it.
17	
18	This file records the escape hatch that the *pointwise* gate opens up.  Because
19	`isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_certified_adaptation` accepts **any**
20	adaptation over the shrunken base, we are free to choose one whose pieces are
21	**support-separated**: each off-diagonal overlap misses the divisor, so its overlap
22	colength vanishes.  For such an adaptation
23	
24	* `δ_left = δ_right` on the nose (`deltaLeft_eq_deltaRight_of_separated`), hence
25	* `W(d)` is the whole product `∏_j colength j` (`gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_separated'`), and
26	* both cokernels are *zero* modules, so (c3)/(c4) hold for free
27	  (`flat_coker_incl_of_separated`, `flat_coker_diff_of_separated`).
28	
29	What remains of the certificate is only the (c1) data — chart-local colengths finite
30	projective — plus the constant-rank reading of their product.  Both are already available:
31	(c1) from the support tube (`SupportTubeFinite.lean`, `SupportTube.lean`) and the rank as a
32	sum of the per-piece ranks (`Module.rankAtStalk_pi`).
33	
34	This is a genuine reduction, not a repackaging: the hypothesis it trades for is the
35	*geometric separation* of the chosen pieces, which the tube produces one base point at a
36	time, whereas the discharged hypotheses were fibrewise flatness statements over a
37	nonreduced base.
38	
39	## Main declarations
40	
41	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_separated'` — the equalizer
42	  collapses over an arbitrary base ring (the field-level lemma generalized).
43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.deltaLeft_eq_deltaRight_of_separated` — the Čech
44	  difference vanishes.
45	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.isCertified_of_separated` — the certificate from
46	  (c1) plus a rank reading, with no kernel-spanning and no flatness input.
47	-/
48	
49	set_option autoImplicit false
50	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
51	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
52	
53	universe u
54	
55	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite
56	
57	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
58	
59	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
60	
61	namespace DivisorAdaptation
62	
63	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))} [IsProper C.hom]
64	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
65	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi]
66	variable {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
67	variable (A : DivisorAdaptation C R pi d)
68	
69	omit [IsProper C.hom]
70	
71	/-- On the diagonal the two overlap-restriction maps coincide: the two `≤`-witnesses
72	`pieces i ⊓ pieces i ≤ pieces i` are definitionally equal (proof irrelevance).  The
73	base-ring form of `DivisorFamilyFieldDegree`'s field-level lemma. -/
74	lemma toOvlLeft_self_eq_toOvlRight_self' (i : A.index) :
75	    A.toOvlLeft i i = A.toOvlRight i i :=
76	  rfl
77	
78	/-- **Support separation collapses the equalizer to the whole product, over any base
79	ring.** If the overlap colength modules vanish off the diagonal, every element of the
80	product of chart-local colengths satisfies the equalizer condition.
81	
82	The field-level statement (`gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_separated`) never used invertibility;
83	this is the same argument over `R`, which is what the DD-R gate consumes. -/
84	lemma gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_separated'
85	    (hsep : ∀ i j : A.index, i ≠ j → Subsingleton (A.ovlColength i j)) :
86	    A.gluedSubmodule = ⊤ := by
87	  refine eq_top_iff.mpr fun s _ => ?_
88	  rw [mem_gluedSubmodule_iff]
89	  rintro ⟨i, j⟩
90	  by_cases hij : i = j
91	  · subst hij
92	    exact congrFun (congrArg (fun f : A.colength i →ₐ[R] A.ovlColength i i => (f : _ → _))
93	      (A.toOvlLeft_self_eq_toOvlRight_self' i)) (s i)
94	  · haveI := hsep i j hij
95	    exact Subsingleton.elim _ _
96	
97	/-- **The Čech difference vanishes for a support-separated adaptation.** Its kernel is the
98	whole product, and a linear map whose kernel is everything is zero. -/
99	lemma deltaLeft_eq_deltaRight_of_separated
100	    (hsep : ∀ i j : A.index, i ≠ j → Subsingleton (A.ovlColength i j)) :
101	    A.deltaLeft = A.deltaRight := by
102	  have h : A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight = 0 := by
103	    rw [← LinearMap.ker_eq_top]
104	    exact A.gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_separated' hsep
105	  exact sub_eq_zero.mp h
106	
107	/-- The equalizer, as a module, is the whole product of chart-local colengths. -/
108	noncomputable def gluedTopEquiv' (h : A.gluedSubmodule = ⊤) : A.Glued ≃ₗ[R] A.chartProd :=
109	  (LinearEquiv.ofEq _ _ h).trans Submodule.topEquiv
110	
111	/-! ## The two flat-cokernel clauses, for free -/
112	
113	/-- (c3) for a support-separated adaptation: the cokernel of `W(d) ↪ ∏_j colength j` is the
114	zero module, because the inclusion is onto. -/
115	lemma flat_coker_incl_of_separated
116	    (hsep : ∀ i j : A.index, i ≠ j → Subsingleton (A.ovlColength i j)) :
117	    Module.Flat R (A.chartProd ⧸ A.gluedSubmodule) := by
118	  haveI : Subsingleton (A.chartProd ⧸ A.gluedSubmodule) := by
119	    rw [A.gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_separated' hsep]
120	    infer_instance
121	  exact Module.Flat.of_linearEquiv
122	    (N := A.chartProd ⧸ A.gluedSubmodule) (M := PUnit.{u+1})
123	    (LinearEquiv.ofSubsingleton _ _)
124	
125	/-- (c4) for a support-separated adaptation: the Čech difference is the zero map, so its
126	range is `⊥` and the cokernel is the overlap product itself — flat as soon as the overlap
127	product is.  In the seed setting that flatness is already landed
128	(`flat_ovlProd_of_seed`). -/
129	lemma flat_coker_diff_of_separated [Module.Flat R A.ovlProd]
130	    (hsep : ∀ i j : A.index, i ≠ j → Subsingleton (A.ovlColength i j)) :
131	    Module.Flat R (A.ovlProd ⧸ LinearMap.range (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight)) := by
132	  have hzero : A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight = 0 :=
133	    sub_eq_zero.mpr (A.deltaLeft_eq_deltaRight_of_separated hsep)
134	  rw [hzero, LinearMap.range_zero]
135	  exact Module.Flat.of_linearEquiv (Submodule.quotEquivOfEqBot ⊥ rfl)
136	
137	/-! ## Separation is a statement about the support, not about the equations
138	
139	The hypothesis `hsep` above is checkable geometrically: an overlap whose points all avoid
140	the family support carries a unit equation, hence a unit overlap ideal, hence a vanishing
141	overlap colength.  In particular an adaptation in which **at most one piece meets the
142	support** is automatically separated. -/
143	
144	/-- **Overlaps that miss the support are separated.** If no point of `pieces i ⊓ pieces j`
145	lies in the support locus, then `A.eqn i` restricts to a unit there (its germ is a unit at
146	every point, `RingedSpace.isUnit_of_isUnit_germ`), so the overlap ideal is the unit ideal
147	and the overlap colength vanishes. -/
148	lemma subsingleton_ovlColength_of_disjoint_supportLocus (i j : A.index)
149	    (hdisj : ∀ z : relCurve C R, z ∈ A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j → z ∉ d.supportLocus) :
150	    Subsingleton (A.ovlColength i j) := by
151	  have hunit : IsUnit (relResAlgHom C R
152	      (inf_le_left : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces i) (A.eqn i)) := by
153	    rw [relResAlgHom_apply]
154	    apply (relCurve C R).toRingedSpace.isUnit_of_isUnit_germ
155	    intro z hz
156	    rw [(relCurve C R).presheaf.germ_res_apply]
157	    have hU : z ∈ d.unitLocus := not_not.mp (hdisj z hz)
158	    exact (A.isUnit_germ_eqn_iff i hz.1).mpr
159	      ((d.mem_unitLocus_iff_isUnit_germ (d.cover.mem_opens z)).mp hU)
160	  have htop : A.ovlIdeal i j = ⊤ :=
161	    Ideal.eq_top_of_isUnit_mem _ (Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_insert _ _)) hunit
162	  exact Ideal.Quotient.subsingleton_iff.mpr htop
163	
164	/-- **One support-meeting piece suffices.** If every piece other than `j₀` avoids the
165	support entirely, the adaptation is separated: any off-diagonal overlap involves a piece
166	missing the support, so the overlap misses it too. -/
167	lemma forall_subsingleton_ovlColength_of_unique_support_piece (j₀ : A.index)
168	    (hother : ∀ j : A.index, j ≠ j₀ →
169	      ∀ z : relCurve C R, z ∈ A.pieces j → z ∉ d.supportLocus) :
170	    ∀ i j : A.index, i ≠ j → Subsingleton (A.ovlColength i j) := by
171	  intro i j hij
172	  refine A.subsingleton_ovlColength_of_disjoint_supportLocus i j fun z hz => ?_
173	  by_cases hi : i = j₀
174	  · exact hother j (by rw [← hi]; exact fun h => hij h.symm) z hz.2
175	  · exact hother i hi z hz.1
176	
177	/-! ## The scope guard: separation forces a fibre-confined support
178	
179	The converse direction bounds this route honestly.  Both pinned charts carry a partition
180	of unity, so a support point lying in `V₀ ⊓ V₁` lies in a piece of **each** chart — an
181	off-diagonal pair whose overlap then meets the support.  Hence a separated adaptation
182	exists only for a system whose support avoids the chart overlap, i.e. is confined to the
183	two vertical fibres of `pi`.  No refinement of the cover repairs this, and the pointwise
184	gate does not help: shrinking the base deletes fibres, it does not move a support point
185	out of `V₀ ⊓ V₁`.
186	
187	The field lane recorded the same obstruction and routed around it
188	(`DivisorFamilyFieldSurj.lean`, deviation note): over a field every module is free, so the
189	certificate is discharged on the plain extraction adaptation instead.  Over a nonreduced
190	base that escape is unavailable, which is exactly why the flat-cokernel content of
191	`DivSchemeHighWindowSyzygy.lean` is unavoidable for a general degree-`g` system. -/
192	
193	/-- **Separation confines the support to the chart overlap's complement.** If a support
194	point `z` lies in both pinned charts, the chart-0 pieces cover `V₀` and the chart-1 pieces
195	cover `V₁`, so `z` lies in a chart-0 piece `i` and a chart-1 piece `j`; these are distinct
196	(`Sum.inl ≠ Sum.inr`), and both equations have non-unit germ at `z`, so the overlap ideal
197	is proper and `ovlColength i j` is **not** subsingleton.
198	
199	So `isCertified_of_separated` applies only to fibre-confined systems.  It is stated to
200	record the scope of the separated route, not to suggest the hypothesis is generic. -/
201	theorem supportLocus_disjoint_chart_inter_of_separated
202	    (hsep : ∀ i j : A.index, i ≠ j → Subsingleton (A.ovlColength i j))
203	    {z : relCurve C R} (hz : z ∈ d.supportLocus)
204	    (hz₀ : z ∈ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover pi)).V₀)
205	    (hz₁ : z ∈ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover pi)).V₁) : False := by
206	  classical
207	  -- the two charts' partitions of unity put `z` in a piece of each chart
208	  obtain ⟨i₀, hi₀⟩ := Opens.mem_iSup.mp (A.toFinCoverData.cover₀ hz₀)
209	  obtain ⟨j₀, hj₀⟩ := Opens.mem_iSup.mp (A.toFinCoverData.cover₁ hz₁)
210	  set i : A.index := Sum.inl i₀ with hi
211	  set j : A.index := Sum.inr j₀ with hj
212	  have hzi : z ∈ A.pieces i := hi₀
213	  have hzj : z ∈ A.pieces j := hj₀
214	  -- the germs of both equations at `z` are non-units, since `z` is in the support
215	  have hnu : ∀ l : A.index, ∀ hzl : z ∈ A.pieces l,
216	      ¬ IsUnit (((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces l) z hzl).hom (A.eqn l)) := by
217	    intro l hzl hu
218	    exact hz ((A.mem_basicOpen_eqn_iff_mem_unitLocus l hzl).mp
219	      (((relCurve C R).mem_basicOpen (A.eqn l) z hzl).mpr hu))
220	  -- but separation makes the overlap colength trivial, i.e. the overlap ideal is `⊤`
221	  haveI := hsep i j (by simp [hi, hj])
222	  have htop : A.ovlIdeal i j = ⊤ := Ideal.Quotient.subsingleton_iff.mp ‹_›
223	  -- evaluating `1 ∈ ovlIdeal i j` at the germ of `z` contradicts non-unitness
224	  have hzW : z ∈ A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j := ⟨hzi, hzj⟩
225	  have hone : (1 : Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j)) ∈ A.ovlIdeal i j := by
226	    rw [htop]; exact Submodule.mem_top
227	  rw [Ideal.mem_span_pair] at hone
228	  obtain ⟨a, b, hab⟩ := hone
229	  -- push the identity into the local ring at `z`
230	  have hgerm := congrArg
231	    (((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j) z hzW).hom) hab
232	  rw [map_one, map_add, map_mul, map_mul] at hgerm
233	  -- both germ images lie in the maximal ideal, so their combination cannot be `1`
234	  have hmi : ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j) z hzW).hom
235	      (relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_left : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces i) (A.eqn i))
236	      ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ((relCurve C R).presheaf.stalk z) := by
237	    rw [relResAlgHom_apply, (relCurve C R).presheaf.germ_res_apply]
238	    exact not_not.mp (fun h => hnu i hzi (IsLocalRing.notMem_maximalIdeal.mp h))
239	  have hmj : ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j) z hzW).hom
240	      (relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_right : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces j) (A.eqn j))
241	      ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ((relCurve C R).presheaf.stalk z) := by
242	    rw [relResAlgHom_apply, (relCurve C R).presheaf.germ_res_apply]
243	    exact not_not.mp (fun h => hnu j hzj (IsLocalRing.notMem_maximalIdeal.mp h))
244	  have hmem : (1 : (relCurve C R).presheaf.stalk z)
245	      ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ((relCurve C R).presheaf.stalk z) := by
246	    rw [← hgerm]
247	    exact Ideal.add_mem _ (Ideal.mul_mem_left _ _ hmi) (Ideal.mul_mem_left _ _ hmj)
248	  exact (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ((relCurve C R).presheaf.stalk z)).ne_top_iff_one.mp
249	    (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal.isMaximal _).ne_top hmem
250	
251	/-- **"At most one piece meets the support" is impossible once the support meets both
252	pinned charts.** This refutes, at the level of the pieces, the shape the `tube-fibre` leaf
253	of the certificate lane was aiming at.
254	
255	A support point `z` of `V₀ ⊓ V₁` lies in a chart-0 piece and a chart-1 piece, and those are
256	distinct — so two distinct pieces meet the support, no matter how the cover is refined. -/
257	theorem not_exists_unique_support_piece
258	    {z : relCurve C R} (hz : z ∈ d.supportLocus)
259	    (hz₀ : z ∈ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover pi)).V₀)
260	    (hz₁ : z ∈ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover pi)).V₁)
261	    (j₀ : A.index)
262	    (hother : ∀ j : A.index, j ≠ j₀ →
263	      ∀ y : relCurve C R, y ∈ A.pieces j → y ∉ d.supportLocus) : False :=
264	  A.supportLocus_disjoint_chart_inter_of_separated
265	    (A.forall_subsingleton_ovlColength_of_unique_support_piece j₀ hother) hz hz₀ hz₁
266	
267	/-! ## The certificate -/
268	
269	/-- **The certificate of a support-separated adaptation.** With the off-diagonal overlap
270	colengths vanishing, the equalizer is the whole product, the Čech difference is zero, and
271	both flat-cokernel clauses hold automatically.  What is left is exactly the (c1) data —
272	each chart-local colength finite projective over `R` — plus the constant-rank reading,
273	which for the product is the sum of the per-piece ranks.
274	
275	This is the shape the pointwise gate can consume: no kernel-spanning hypothesis, and no
276	flatness of a Čech cokernel over a possibly nonreduced base. -/
277	theorem isCertified_of_separated {n : ℕ} [Module.Flat R A.ovlProd]
278	    (hsep : ∀ i j : A.index, i ≠ j → Subsingleton (A.ovlColength i j))
279	    (hfin : ∀ j, Module.Finite R (A.colength j))
280	    (hproj : ∀ j, Module.Projective R (A.colength j))
281	    (hrank : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
282	      ∑ᶠ j : A.index, Module.rankAtStalk (R := R) (A.colength j) p = n) :
283	    A.IsCertified n := by
284	  classical
285	  haveI := hfin
286	  haveI := hproj
287	  haveI : ∀ j : A.index, Module.Flat R (A.colength j) := fun _ =>
288	    Module.Flat.of_projective
289	  have htop := A.gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_separated' hsep
290	  have hequiv : A.Glued ≃ₗ[R] A.chartProd := A.gluedTopEquiv' htop
291	  haveI hprodProj : Module.Projective R A.chartProd :=
292	    Module.Projective.of_equiv' (P := A.chartProd)
293	      (DirectSum.linearEquivFunOnFintype R A.index (fun j => A.colength j))
294	  refine
295	    { finite_colength := hfin
296	      projective_colength := hproj
297	      finite_glued := Module.Finite.equiv hequiv.symm
298	      projective_glued := Module.Projective.of_equiv' (P := A.Glued) hequiv.symm
299	      rankAtStalk_glued := fun p => ?_
300	      flat_coker_incl := A.flat_coker_incl_of_separated hsep
301	      flat_coker_diff := A.flat_coker_diff_of_separated hsep }
302	  rw [Module.rankAtStalk_eq_of_equiv hequiv, Module.rankAtStalk_pi]
303	  exact hrank p
304	
305	end DivisorAdaptation
306	
307	end AlgebraicGeometry

9	/-!
10	# No-leak over a shrunken base, with no fibre hypothesis
11	
12	The certificate assemblers consume, per piece `j`, the fibrewise clause
13	
14	`∀ s, (fibre over s) ∩ closure (supp ∩ pieces j) ⊆ pieces j`
15	
16	(`isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning`), equivalently emptiness of the **leak locus**
17	`supportLeak (pieces j) = closure (supp ∩ pieces j) \ pieces j`
18	(`Scheme.LocalEquations.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty`).
19	
20	The `tube-fibre` leaf of the DD-R lane tried to obtain this by putting the whole support
21	inside a single piece.  That shape is refuted — `DivSchemeCertZarSep.lean`,
22	`not_exists_unique_support_piece`: both pinned charts carry a partition of unity, so a
23	support point of `V₀ ⊓ V₁` always lies in two distinct pieces.
24	
25	This file gets the clause a different way, and **without any fibre analysis**.  The leak
26	locus is closed, and under a universally closed structure morphism its base image is closed
27	too (`isClosed_image_supportLeak`).  So:
28	
29	* over the *open complement* of that base image, nothing leaks;
30	* that complement is a Zariski neighbourhood of every base point it contains, refinable to a
31	  basic open — the `Localization.Away` shape the pointwise gate consumes.
32	
33	The leak locus is a genuine obstruction only over its own base image, which is a **closed**
34	subset of `Spec R`. So the no-leak clause is available on a Zariski-dense open of the base
35	for free; what a fibre analysis is still needed for is the base points *inside* that closed
36	image.
37	
38	## Main declarations
39	
40	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.exists_basicOpen_supportLeak_eq_empty` — a basic
41	  open around any base point outside the leak's image, over which nothing leaks.
42	* `Scheme.LocalEquations.forall_fibre_closure_subset_of_supportLeak_inter_eq_empty` —
43	  leak-freeness over an open of the base gives the assembler's fibrewise clause there.
44	-/
45	
46	set_option autoImplicit false
47	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
48	
49	universe u
50	
51	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite
52	open scoped TensorProduct
53	
54	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
55	
56	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
57	
58	/-! ## The idempotent brick
59	
60	I-0209 predicted the shape of the missing construction: the canonical idempotents of a
61	finite projective colength algebra split the divisor scheme into packets, and a piece
62	swallowing a packet has a clopen trace, hence carries the certificate.  The algebraic core
63	of that is elementary and is recorded here: cutting by an idempotent produces a **direct
64	summand**, so projectivity is inherited with no flatness or finiteness input. -/
65	
66	section Idempotent
67	
68	variable {R B : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing B] [Algebra R B]
69	
70	set_option maxHeartbeats 1000000 in
71	-- The `Ideal`-to-`Submodule` coercion in the quotient makes `liftQ` elaboration expensive.
72	/-- **Cutting by an idempotent gives a direct summand.** For `e` idempotent, multiplication
73	by `e` is a well-defined `R`-linear section of `B ↠ B ⧸ (1 - e)`, so the quotient is a
74	retract of `B` and inherits projectivity.
75	
76	This is the algebraic core of the packet-splitting construction I-0209 asks for: an
77	idempotent of the colength algebra cuts out a clopen packet, and the corresponding quotient
78	is projective for free. -/
79	theorem Module.Projective.quotient_span_singleton_one_sub_of_isIdempotentElem
80	    [Module.Projective R B] (e : B) (he : IsIdempotentElem e) :
81	    Module.Projective R (B ⧸ (Ideal.span {1 - e}).restrictScalars R) := by
82	  set P := (Ideal.span {1 - e}).restrictScalars R with hP
83	  set s : (B ⧸ P) →ₗ[R] B :=
84	    P.liftQ (LinearMap.mulLeft R e) (by
85	      intro x hx
86	      have hx' : x ∈ Ideal.span {1 - e} := hx
87	      rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton] at hx'
88	      obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := hx'

name: horizon
description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
---

You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.

## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate

Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.

You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
**shared state**, not meetings:

- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
  another team.
- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).

Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
commands (unread inbox for your task, your session's runtime/tokens, other live
runs) — read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone.

## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)

**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.

The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):

- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.

## Your session's identity (environment variables)

The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |

## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)

Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:

- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).

## One-shot discipline (important)

This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).

## Pick the highest-value work

Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.

If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
the objective is large. Leave a `"$HORIZON_BIN" task comment <task_id> --body …`
at each significant step. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
(it returns to the queue).

## Fresh-context checkpoints

The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
checkpoints:

- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
  clean/build result.

Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
terminal `done` claim.

Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.

## Warnings are work

Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
why.

Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
issue rather than repeated no-op calls.

## Do the work (Lean)

For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
configured final build covers the same files.

**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
